It differs from sibling techniques by combining visibility culling and LOD selection into a single recursive traversal, deferring geometry queueing until a node is determined to be either fully visible at its current LOD or fully outside the frustum [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a recursive traversal of an octree. It details the logic for frustum culling (visibility culling) and distance-based LOD selection within the same recursive function (`octree_cull`). The code shows that geometry is only enqueued (`queue_gsvl`, `queue_mesh`) when a specific condition is met: `if( distance > lod*(1024) )`. This condition implies that if the node is visible (passed frustum cull) and the distance threshold is met (LOD selection logic), the geometry is queued. If the distance is not met, the LOD is decremented and recursion continues. This matches the claim's description of combining visibility culling and LOD selection into a single recursive traversal and deferring queueing until a node is determined to be fully visible at its current LOD (or outside, in which case it returns early).
